blind_target.authors: Panoutsopoulou K, Metrustry S, Doherty SA, Laslett LL, Maciewicz RA, Hart DJ, et al.
blind_target.title: The effect of FTO variation on increased osteoarthritis risk is mediated through body mass index: a mendelian randomisation study
blind_target.evidence_quote: An extended study of the GWAS study revealed that the association between rs8044769 and OA was degenerated after stratification by BMI, and the association between rs8044769 and BMI was identified in this study [14].
blind_target.outcome_quote: An extended study of the GWAS study revealed that the association between rs8044769 and OA was degenerated after stratification by BMI, and the association between rs8044769 and BMI was identified in this study [14]. There have been several reports for the association between FTO and BMI [6–12], and two of them referred to rs8044769 as BMI associated SNP [11, 12]. So, we suspected that the association between rs8044769 and BMI may contribute to the association between this SNP and OA in the GWAS study. However, in our study, rs8044769 was not associated with BMI, and it might be another reason for the negative association between rs8044769 and OA.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The extended GWAS paper is explicitly compared on the SNP–BMI association; the current study fails to find that association.

blind_target.authors: Zhao J, Bradfield JP, Li M, Wang K, Zhang H, Kim CE, et al.
blind_target.title: The role of obesity-associated loci identified in genome-wide association studies in the determination of pediatric BMI
blind_target.evidence_quote: The association of the FTO polymorphism (rs8044769) with BMI was not replicated in the Chinese Han population either. The previous studies showed that FTO was associated with BMI [6–12], and two of them referred to rs8044769 as BMI-associated SNP [11, 12]. In the association analysis of rs8044769 with BMI, we found no association between rs8044769 and BMI.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The association of the FTO polymorphism (rs8044769) with BMI was not replicated in the Chinese Han population either. The previous studies showed that FTO was associated with BMI [6–12], and two of them referred to rs8044769 as BMI-associated SNP [11, 12]. In the association analysis of rs8044769 with BMI, we found no association between rs8044769 and BMI.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly identify references 11 and 12 as reports of the exact rs8044769–BMI association and state that this association was not replicated. Other FTO variants in references 6–10 are background.

blind_target.authors: Wang Y, Chu M, Rong J, Xing B, Zhu L, Zhao Y, et al.
blind_target.title: No association of the single nucleotide polymorphism rs8044769 in the fat mass and obesity-associated gene with knee osteoarthritis risk and body mass index: a population-based study in China
blind_target.evidence_quote: A study on Chinese Han population denied this association, but the subject number of the Chinese study was a little bit small [16]. Until now, the association between FTO and OA remains debatable.Therefore, we evaluated the potential association of the FTO polymorphism (rs8044769) with OA in the Chinese Han population with more cases and controls.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Our results were consistent with a previous study in Chinese population and had enlarged studied subjects. We also conducted a meta-analysis together with the previous study in Chinese population to offer a solid evidence that rs8044769 of FTO was not associated with OA risk or BMI in Chinese population.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The explicitly motivated larger Chinese sample re-tests the earlier Chinese null and agrees. The new sample independently re-tests this finding; the accompanying pooled meta-analysis is not the sole basis.
